MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Medical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Sex: Female
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRING PHYSICIAN
[redacted name], MD
[redacted location] Hospital

CLINICAL INDICATION
Adult female with complex multisystem disorder including intellectual disability, delayed motor development, diabetes insipidus, pericentral retinitis pigmentosa, ptosis, exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, proximal tubulopathy, seizures, ataxia, thenar/hypothenar abnormalities, primary amenorrhea, premature ovarian insufficiency, myopia, and episodic vomiting. Previous whole genome sequencing performed through national genomic research initiative identified variants requiring clinical confirmation.

TEST PERFORMED
Sanger sequencing confirmation of variants in PMM2, AQP2, and CACNA1A genes

METHODOLOGY
Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood using standard protocols. PCR amplification and bidirectional Sanger sequencing were performed for the following regions:
- PMM2 (NM_000303.3): Exons 3 and 5
- AQP2 (NM_000486.6): Exons 1 and 4
- CACNA1A (NM_001127221.2): Exon 4

Sequencing was performed on an Applied Biosystems 3730xl DNA Analyzer. Data analysis was performed using Mutation Surveyor software v5.1.2.

RESULTS

PROBAND RESULTS:

1. PMM2 (NM_000303.3)
   - c.305A>G p.(Tyr102Cys) - HETEROZYGOUS
     Classification: Likely Pathogenic
     Located in exon 3
   - c.442G>A p.(Asp148Asn) - HETEROZYGOUS
     Classification: Pathogenic
     Located in exon 5

2. AQP2 (NM_000486.6)
   - c.707_720dup p.(Glu241fs) - HETEROZYGOUS
     Classification: Likely Pathogenic
     14bp duplication in exon 4 causing frameshift
   - c.34G>A p.(Ala12Thr) - HETEROZYGOUS
     Classification: Variant of Uncertain Significance (VUS)
     Located in exon 1

3. CACNA1A (NM_001127221.2)
   - c.359A>G p.(His120Arg) - HETEROZYGOUS
     Classification: Variant of Uncertain Significance (VUS)
     Located in exon 4

MATERNAL RESULTS:

1. PMM2 (NM_000303.3)
   - c.305A>G p.(Tyr102Cys) - NOT DETECTED
   - c.442G>A p.(Asp148Asn) - HETEROZYGOUS

2. AQP2 (NM_000486.6)
   - c.707_720dup p.(Glu241fs) - HETEROZYGOUS
   - c.34G>A p.(Ala12Thr) - NOT DETECTED

3. CACNA1A (NM_001127221.2)
   - c.359A>G p.(His120Arg) - NOT DETECTED

INTERPRETATION

PMM2 Analysis:
The proband carries two heterozygous variants in PMM2. The c.442G>A p.(Asp148Asn) variant is a well-established pathogenic variant associated with congenital disorder of glycosylation type Ia (PMM2-CDG). The c.305A>G p.(Tyr102Cys) variant is classified as likely pathogenic based on computational predictions and rarity in population databases. The mother carries only the c.442G>A variant, indicating the c.305A>G variant was either inherited from the father or arose de novo. Phase determination is required to confirm these variants are in trans (on opposite chromosomes), which would be consistent with autosomal recessive PMM2-CDG.

AQP2 Analysis:
The proband carries a likely pathogenic frameshift variant (c.707_720dup) and a VUS (c.34G>A). The frameshift variant is predicted to result in premature protein truncation and is consistent with nephrogenic diabetes insipidus. The mother also carries the frameshift variant. The c.34G>A variant's clinical significance remains uncertain. AQP2-related nephrogenic diabetes insipidus typically follows autosomal recessive inheritance, though dominant forms exist.

CACNA1A Analysis:
The c.359A>G p.(His120Arg) variant is classified as a VUS. This variant has insufficient evidence to determine pathogenicity. CACNA1A variants are associated with episodic ataxia type 2, familial hemiplegic migraine, and spinocerebellar ataxia type 6. The variant was not detected in the mother.

CLINICAL CORRELATION
The genetic findings provide molecular support for several of the proband's clinical features:
- PMM2 variants (if confirmed in trans) explain the multisystem features consistent with PMM2-CDG
- AQP2 frameshift variant supports the diabetes insipidus diagnosis
- CACNA1A VUS requires additional evidence to determine relevance to ataxia and seizures

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Paternal testing is strongly recommended to:
   - Determine phase of PMM2 variants (confirm trans configuration)
   - Assess inheritance of AQP2 c.34G>A variant
   - Determine inheritance of CACNA1A variant

2. Transferrin isoelectric focusing or carbohydrate-deficient transferrin analysis to support PMM2-CDG diagnosis

3. Genetic counseling to discuss:
   - Inheritance patterns and recurrence risks
   - Implications for family members
   - Available carrier testing for at-risk relatives

4. Consider functional studies for VUS interpretation if clinically indicated

5. Periodic variant reclassification review as new evidence emerges

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Medical Center Molecular Genetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the FDA.

Laboratory Director
[redacted date]
